blocks.content: The asteroid belt separates the inner terrestrial planets from the outer Jovian giants, marking a fundamental transition in density and atmospheric composition across our solar system.

rows: Few or no natural moons; No rings
Numerous natural moons; Ring systems present

items: Venus and Uranus rotate from East to West (retrograde rotation), whereas all other planets rotate from West to East.
Venus is the hottest planet in the Solar System due to a runaway greenhouse effect driven by an atmospheric CO2 concentration of over 95%.
The Asteroid Belt lies strictly between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter.
Saturn has the lowest overall density among all planets—less than that of water.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Planets are divided into Inner (Terrestrial) planets—Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars—and Outer (Jovian) planets—Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.
Terrestrial planets have high densities, rocky surfaces, solid mantles, and few or no natural satellites.
Jovian planets are giant gas spheres composed primarily of hydrogen and helium, featuring low densities, numerous moons, and ring systems.
The Asteroid Belt forms a distinct physical boundary located between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter.
In August 2006, the International Astronomical Union (IAU) redefined a planet, reclassifying Pluto as a dwarf planet.
